title: Claude Code documentation outranks the course material on all four conflicts
context: The Anthropic subagents and skills courses and the Claude Code documentation disagree in four places. The user directed that documentation wins because it is more current. Each resolution is load-bearing for a later section of the SPEC, so they are recorded rather than silently applied.
options: Follow the course, which is more prescriptive and worked-example driven
Follow the documentation on every conflict
Merge both and annotate the disagreements case by case
outcome: Documentation wins on all four. C1, the dangerous one: the course says allowed-tools restricts which tools a skill may use, and the docs say it does not restrict — every tool remains callable and the grant clears at the next user message. Building a read-only skill on allowed-tools would have produced a guardrail that does not hold, which is the exact failure the SPEC exists to remove; skill rule K6 now forbids using it as a restriction. C2: name is optional on a skill and defaults to the directory name. C3: no blanket restart is needed, since Claude Code watches the agents and skills directories, so a restart is required only after settings and hooks change. C4: the fork subagent type exists as a first-class vehicle that the course omits entirely, and it is central to the target architecture.
